chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee' from Abi Ismail al-Sarraj from Yahya ibn Ma'mar al-Attar from Abi Basir from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Four thousand angels, with disheveled hair and covered in dust, mourn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) until the Day of Resurrection. No one comes to him except that they welcome him, and no one leaves except that they accompany him. He does not fall ill except that they visit him, and he does not die except that they attend his funeral.

key_terms.اسْتَقْبَلُوهُ: They welcome him (face him upon arrival)

ai.seo_question: What do the angels do at the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq narrates that four thousand specific angels, distinguished by their disheveled hair and dusty appearance, continuously mourn Imam Husayn (a.s.) at his grave until the Day of Judgment. These angels actively engage with visitors by welcoming them, accompanying them upon departure, visiting during illness, and attending the funeral, highlighting the perpetual spiritual vitality of the Imam's resting place. This tradition underscores the concept of 'Hadarat al-Mawla' (the presence of the Master) in Shia theology, where the grave is not a place of absence but of active, angelic witness and connection.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 18. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to us by Abdillah b. Ja’far al-Himyari who said it was narrated to us by Muhammad b. al-Hussain from Muhammad b. Ismail b. Bazee’ from Abi Ismail al-Sarraj from Yahya b. Mu’ammar al-’Attar from Abi Basir from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “

Four thousand angels are appointed at the grave of Imam Husain (a.s.) with their hair covered in mud and in a distressed state. They will mourn Imam Husain (a.s.) till the Day of Judgment. They welcome whoever comes for the Ziyarat and that person does not return until they accompany him. He does not fall ill but that they come to treat him. He does not die but that they attend his funeral prayer.”
